code.title: Shape Area Through Abstract Base
code.description:
Abstract classes define a contract without implementation. Shape declares a pure virtual area() = 0 and can never be created itself; Circle and Square inherit and each supply the real area formula. Read the shape code and its size, build the right object through a Shape pointer, and print the polymorphic area with two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with a character (C for circle, S for square) and one number: the radius for C or the side for S.

Output Format:
Area: <value with exactly 2 decimals>

Constraints:
Code is C or S; 1 <= size <= 1000.
code.inputconstrains: Code is C or S; 1 <= size <= 1000

code.title: Animal Sounds via Pure Virtual
code.description:
Every pet answers differently, yet the kennel desk treats them all as one type. Animal declares a pure virtual speak(); Dog and Cat each override it with their own sound. Read the pet code and name, create the matching animal through an Animal pointer, and make it speak polymorphically.

Input Format:
One line with a character (D for dog, C for cat) and the pet's name (single word).

Output Format:
<name> says <sound>   (Dog says Woof, Cat says Meow)

Constraints:
Code is D or C; 1 <= name length <= 20.
code.inputconstrains: Code is D or C; 1 <= name length <= 20

code.title: Abstract Machine Work Report
code.description:
An abstract class can mix ready-made behaviour with pure contracts. Machine provides the concrete method ready() that prints 'Machine ready', while work() stays pure virtual. Printer and Scanner complete the contract with their own work lines. Read the machine code and unit number, then print both the shared concrete step and the derived step.

Input Format:
One line with a character (P for printer, S for scanner) and an integer unit number.

Output Format:
Machine ready
<work line> on unit <unit>   (Printing job for P, Scanning page for S)

Constraints:
Code is P or S; 1 <= unit <= 1000.
code.inputconstrains: Code is P or S; 1 <= unit <= 1000
code.output1:
Machine ready
Printing job on unit 1
code.output2:
Machine ready
Scanning page on unit 99
code.output3:
Machine ready
Printing job on unit 1000
code.sampleoutput1:
Machine ready
Printing job on unit 7
code.sampleoutput2:
Machine ready
Scanning page on unit 3

code.title: Abstract Employee Salary Desk
code.description:
A payroll desk treats every worker as an Employee but pays them differently. The abstract Employee class declares pure virtual salary(); a Manager adds a bonus to a fixed base, a Worker multiplies hourly rate by hours worked. Read the employee code, create the right object through an Employee pointer and print the computed salary.

Input Format:
One line starting with a character: M followed by base and bonus, or W followed by rate and hours (all integers).

Output Format:
Salary: <computed salary>

Constraints:
1 <= each value <= 1000000; code is M or W.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= each value <= 1000000; code is M or W

code.title: Interface Encoder Pair
code.description:
An interface is a class made only of pure virtual functions — a pure contract with no data and no bodies. Encoder declares pure virtual encode(n) and nothing else; DoubleEncoder returns twice the number and SquareEncoder returns its square. Read the implementation code and the number, then print the encoded value through the interface pointer.

Input Format:
One line with a character (D for double encoder, S for square encoder) and an integer n.

Output Format:
Encoded: <result>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000; code is D or S.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100000; code is D or S

code.title: Vehicle Fleet Wheel Counter
code.description:
A fleet desk counts wheels without caring which vehicle parks where. The abstract Vehicle class declares pure virtual wheels() returning an int; Car has 4, Bike has 2 and Auto has 3. Read the vehicle code and the fleet size, then print the total wheel count using polymorphism.

Input Format:
One line with a character (C for car, B for bike, A for auto) and an integer count of vehicles.

Output Format:
Total wheels: <wheels per vehicle * count>

Constraints:
Code is C, B or A; 1 <= count <= 1000.
code.inputconstrains: Code is C, B or A; 1 <= count <= 1000

code.title: Checkout Payment Gateway Interface
code.description:
Online checkouts settle money through a payment interface. Pay is a pure interface with only pure virtual functions; charge(amount) returns what the customer actually pays. CardPay adds a 2 percent gateway fee (amount + amount/50) while UPIPay applies a 1 percent instant cashback (amount - amount/100). Read the mode code and the amount, then print the payable figure.

Input Format:
One line with a character (C for card, U for UPI) and an integer amount.

Output Format:
Payable: <amount returned by charge>

Constraints:
100 <= amount <= 1000000; code is C or U.
code.inputconstrains: 100 <= amount <= 1000000; code is C or U

code.title: Alert Broadcast Interface
code.description:
A monitoring hub broadcasts alerts through a notification interface. Notifier declares pure virtual send(msg) and nothing else; EmailAlert prints an EMAIL line and SMSAlert prints an SMS line. Read the channel code, then the whole message line (it may contain spaces), and dispatch polymorphically through the interface pointer.

Input Format:
First a character (E for email, S for SMS), then after one space (or on the next line) the message text.

Output Format:
EMAIL: <message>
or
SMS: <message>

Constraints:
Code is E or S; 1 <= message length <= 60.
code.inputconstrains: Code is E or S; 1 <= message length <= 60

code.title: Storage Backend Interface Report
code.description:
A backup tool saves files either on a local drive or in the cloud behind one storage interface. Storage declares pure virtual save(mb) and nothing else; LocalDrive consumes exactly mb megabytes while CloudDrive compresses to half (mb / 2). Read the backend code and the file size, then report the space used.

Input Format:
One line with a character (L for local, C for cloud) and an integer size in MB.

Output Format:
Used: <mb consumed by the chosen backend> MB

Constraints:
1 <= size <= 1000000; code is L or C.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= size <= 1000000; code is L or C

code.title: Commute Fare Interface Counter
code.description:
Daily commutes can be billed through a fare interface. Fare declares pure virtual fare(km); BusFare charges 5 rupees per kilometre flat, MetroFare charges a 10 rupee base plus 3 rupees per kilometre. Read the mode code and the distance, then print the fare through the interface pointer.

Input Format:
One line with a character (B for bus, M for metro) and an integer distance in km.

Output Format:
Fare: <fare> rupees

Constraints:
1 <= km <= 1000; code is B or M.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= km <= 1000; code is B or M

code.title: Protected Base Report Builder
code.description:
Abstract bases can do real work for their children. Invoice stores items and rate in protected members, exposes the concrete helper subtotal() = items * rate, and leaves total() pure virtual. GSTInvoice finishes the job by adding 18 percent tax (subtotal * 18 / 100); DiscountInvoice removes 10 percent (subtotal / 10). Read the invoice code and numbers, then print the base-computed subtotal and the derived-computed total.

Input Format:
One line with a character (G for GST invoice, D for discount invoice), an integer item count and an integer rate per item.

Output Format:
Subtotal: <items * rate>
Total: <total computed by the derived class>

Constraints:
1 <= items <= 10000; 1 <= rate <= 100000; code is G or D.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= items <= 10000; 1 <= rate <= 100000; code is G or D

code.title: Deleting Through the Base Pointer
code.description:
A memory auditor deletes cache objects only through the abstract base pointer. Cache declares pure virtual size() and a virtual destructor that prints the base release line; RamCache and DiskCache print their own construction and teardown lines, and the derived destructor always runs before the base one when the destructor is virtual. Read the cache code, attach the cache, report its blocks and delete it through the base pointer to prove the virtual destructor chain.

Input Format:
One line with a character (R for ram cache, D for disk cache).

Output Format:
For R: [+] ram cache attached / [i] blocks in use: 8 / Deleting through base pointer... / [-] ram cache flushed / [-] cache base released / Audit complete: no leaks
For D: same flow with disk cache attached, blocks 64 and disk cache synced

Constraints:
Code is R or D.
code.inputconstrains: Code is R or D
code.output1:
[+] disk cache attached
[i] blocks in use: 64
Deleting through base pointer...
[-] disk cache synced
[-] cache base released
Audit complete: no leaks
code.output2:

Deleting through base pointer...
[-] ram cache flushed
[-] cache base released
Audit complete: no leaks
code.output3:

code.title: Pure Virtual Default Recipe
code.description:
Pure virtual functions are allowed to have bodies. Brew keeps brew(cups) = 0 yet still defines Brew::brew(cups) with the shared 'Boiling water' step; derived classes override brew() and deliberately call the pure virtual body through the class-name syntax Brew::brew(cups) before adding their own ingredient line. Read the drink code and cup count, then print the shared step followed by the derived step.

Input Format:
One line with a character (T for tea, C for coffee) and an integer number of cups.

Output Format:
Boiling water for <cups> cup(s)
Adding tea leaves for <cups> cup(s)   (or: Adding coffee powder for <cups> cup(s))

Constraints:
1 <= cups <= 100; code is T or C.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= cups <= 100; code is T or C
code.output1:
Boiling water for 5 cup(s)
Adding coffee powder for 5 cup(s)
code.output2:
Boiling water for 10 cup(s)
Adding tea leaves for 10 cup(s)
code.output3:
Boiling water for 3 cup(s)
Adding coffee powder for 3 cup(s)
code.sampleoutput1:
Boiling water for 2 cup(s)
Adding tea leaves for 2 cup(s)
code.sampleoutput2:
Boiling water for 1 cup(s)
Adding coffee powder for 1 cup(s)

code.title: Unit Converter Framework Desk
code.description:
Measurement tools share one conversion framework. UnitConverter is an abstract class with pure virtual convert(value); KmToMiles multiplies by 0.621371 and KgToPounds multiplies by 2.20462. Read the converter code and the value, build the right converter through the base pointer and print the result with two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with a character (K for km to miles, P for kg to pounds) and a number value.

Output Format:
Converted: <value with exactly 2 decimals>

Constraints:
0.5 <= value <= 100000; code is K or P.
code.inputconstrains: 0.5 <= value <= 100000; code is K or P

code.title: Shape Composer Total Area
code.description:
A canvas composer assembles shapes from a build list and bills the whole canvas. Shape is abstract with pure virtual area() and name(); Circle and Square implement both. Read N shapes (C radius or S side), park them in an array of Shape pointers, then walk the list polymorphically printing each shape's name and area, and finish with the sum of all areas.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a character (C or S) and a number (radius or side).

Output Format:
For each shape in input order: <Circle or Square> area: <value with 2 decimals>
Last line: Total area: <sum with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100; 1 <= size <= 1000.

code.title: Printable Scannable Office Copier
code.description:
Interface segregation keeps contracts small and focused. Printable declares pure virtual print(doc, pages) and Scannable declares pure virtual scan(doc, pages). A single Copier class implements BOTH interfaces, and main talks to it through two different interface pointers, exercising one capability each. Read the document name and page count, then print both capability lines.

Input Format:
One line with a document name (single word) and an integer page count.

Output Format:
Printing <doc> (pages: <pages>)
Scanning <doc> (pages: <pages>)

Constraints:
1 <= pages <= 500; 1 <= name length <= 20.
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= pages <= 500; 1 <= name length <= 20

code.title: Device Lifecycle Template Runner
code.description:
A data centre controller boots and stops many kinds of equipment through one template method. The abstract Device class provides the concrete run() skeleton which calls the pure virtual steps boot() and shutdown() in a fixed order; ConsoleDevice and NetworkDevice supply their own lifecycle lines carrying their device id. Read N commands, build each requested device polymorphically, run its cycle, free it, then print the handling summary.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a device kind (console or network) and an integer device id.

Output Format:
Per device:
[boot] <kind>-<id> up
[run] cycle complete
[shutdown] <kind>-<id> down
Final line: All devices handled: <N>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100; 1 <= id <= 100000.

code.title: Payroll Compensation Policy Engine
code.description:
A startup payroll engine pays every employee through one abstract Compensation contract. compute() stays pure virtual and each policy completes it its own way: MonthlyPay returns a fixed salary, HourlyPay multiplies rate by hours, CommissionPay adds sales * percent / 100 to a base. The shared report() in the base class calls compute() polymorphically to print one line per employee, and the engine closes with the payroll total.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: policy code (M, H or C), a name (single word), then the policy numbers — M: salary; H: rate hours; C: base sales percent.

Output Format:
Per employee: <name> earns <amount>
Final line: Payroll total: <sum of all amounts>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50; 1 <= every number <= 10000000; code is M, H or C.

code.title: Polymorphic Cleanup Manifest
code.description:
A hosting platform must release every asset cleanly through the abstract base pointer. Asset tracks a static alive counter, keeps tag() pure virtual and owns the virtual destructor that decrements the counter; LandAsset, SeaAsset and AirAsset print their own creation and releasing lines. Read N assets, watch them register, then delete them newest-first through Asset pointers and print the audit summary proving the virtual destructor chain ran for every object.

Input Format:
First line: N. Next N lines: a type code (L, S or A) and an integer id.

Output Format:
Per asset: [created] <land|sea|air>-<id>
Then: [cleanup start] <N> assets
Then, newest first: [releasing] <land|sea|air>-<id>
Finally: [audit] remaining: 0 and [audit] released: <N>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100; 1 <= id <= 100000; code is L, S or A.

code.title: Plugin Registry Pipeline Report
code.description:
A text pipeline loads two plugins behind one registry interface. Plugin declares pure virtual name() and execute(data) and nothing else; SumPlugin totals the data while MaxPlugin reports the largest value. The registry walks every plugin polymorphically, prints name and result, records the executed names in order, and finally frees each plugin through the interface pointer.

Input Format:
First line: N (data count). Second line: N integers (may be negative).

Output Format:
Plugin <name> -> <result>   (once per plugin: sum then max)
Executed: <comma-joined names in registry order>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000; -1000000 <= each value <= 1000000.

mcqs.title: Why Virtual Destructors Matter
mcqs.description: A program deletes derived objects through a base class pointer. Why must the base destructor be virtual?
mcqs.Option1: So memory is freed twice as fast

mcqs.Option4: So the compiler removes the need for delete

mcqs.title: One Pure Virtual Makes It Abstract

mcqs.Option4: It can be instantiated but the missing calls crash
